bug_semantics: A pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL for the module-level callable profile.run is parsed as module="profile", name="run". PickleScan classified a global as an issue only when the module appeared in its manually enumerated unsafe map and the extracted name exactly matched that module's filter (or the filter was "*"). The original map omitted profile entirely; a later attempted hardening used {"Profile.run", "Profile.runctx"}, which still could not match the extracted module-level names "run" and "runctx". Thus a malicious pickle could produce zero issues and then profile.run(statement) would reach Profile.run and exec(statement) when unpickled.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the first PickleScan implementation: it introduced an exact-name, manually enumerated dangerous-global filter without any entry for Python's profile module. That made profile.run executable but undetected from the scanner's first release lineage. Commit aecd11be98702caa9ba9b12189d91ad596a36114 later added class-qualified profile names, but it was not the BIC because its immediate parent already allowed the same module-level profile.run payload; it only preserved the pre-existing omission as a name-shape mismatch.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e shows human author and committer Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre314@users.noreply.github.com>, subject/body "Implement Pickle scanner", and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/security/advisories/GHSA-7wx9-6375-f5wh documents the profile.run pickle as module=profile/name=run, zero scanner issues, and execution through exec(), with affected range <1.0.4 and patched version 1.0.4. `git log --all --reverse -- src/picklescan/scanner.py` identifies c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e as the first commit of that file. `git show c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e -- src/picklescan/scanner.py` shows the file created from /dev/null, a finite `_suspicious_globals` with no profile entry, GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL extraction into `(module, name)`, and exact `g[1] in filter` issue counting. Direct parent-tree check `git cat-file -e 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326:src/picklescan/scanner.py` fails because the scanner file does not exist in the parent, proving absence of the vulnerable scanner mechanism. `git log -L '/"profile"/,+1':src/picklescan/scanner.py` shows aecd11be98702caa9ba9b12189d91ad596a36114 later added `"profile": {"Profile.run", "Profile.runctx"}` and bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb replaced it with `"profile": "*"`; direct inspection of aecd's parent 7f994d62084fe43f1cffdef2f9bae6923344ef53 shows no profile entry, so aecd did not first make profile.run pass. `git describe --tags --contains c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e` returns v0.0.2~12, placing the BIC before the earliest available v0.0.2 tag. Tag enumeration places every later pre-fix release through v1.0.3 on that lineage; `git describe --tags --exact-match b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c` returns v1.0.3. `git show bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb` directly changes profile to `*`, adds the GHSA-7wx9-6375-f5wh profile.run regression fixture/assertion, and bumps setup.cfg from 1.0.3 to 1.0.4; `git describe --tags --exact-match bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb` returns v1.0.4. The fix and direct fix are therefore the same commit.
reasoning: The vulnerability existed as soon as PickleScan began deciding danger through a closed module/name list: profile.run was a stable executable pickle global, but the first scanner implementation neither listed profile nor had a generic rule that would count it as an issue. The 2025 class-method advisory work is an important lifecycle event, not the causal introduction: adding class-qualified names left the already-working module-level payload unaffected because the classifier compares the extracted name exactly. The smallest causal BIC is consequently the initial scanner commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e, not the later attempted hardening or the aggregate fix. Its immediate parent contains no scanner file, so the mechanism is directly absent there, and the BIC precedes the earliest repository release tag. The direct 1.0.4 fix broadens the profile module filter to `*` and lands exactly at the advisory's patched boundary. Inspection of only the selected BIC's commit object found no AI authorship/co-authorship marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
